1000462.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Venetan Montenegro (“Montenegro; literally “black mountain””), from mónte (“mountain”) + negro (“black”), a calque of Serbo-Croatian Cȓnā Gòra (“Montenegro; literally “black mountain””), referring to Mount Lovćen. The corresponding Italian form Montenegro became the international name.
The first element derives from Latin montem (“mountain”), the accusative singular of mōns (“mountain”), while the second derives from Latin nigrum (“black”), the accusative masculine singular of niger (“black”).
Compare the parallel borrowings Norwegian Nynorsk Montenegro, Danish Monte

1005070.etyen:
An old river name belonging to the Nordic group of names in -und. Traditionally analysed as deriving from Old Norse brim (“surf, breakers”) with the ancient derivational ending -und, referring to the sound or appearance of rushing water and thus approximately meaning “the one with much splashing and roaring”. Oluf Rygh tentatively reconstructed an earlier form *Brimund.
